text:
tom: FYI — ZenithHealth is ready to sign a 12-month reserved commit but wants a validated capacity plan. They expect bursty traffic: baseline ~2.5k req/min, occasional peaks to 15k req/min for 10-15 minutes. Primary use: short chat responses, avg 18 tokens. Want p95 < 250ms. Can we propose reserved GPUs + a burst strategy and a short preheat/runbook?

anya: Important to separate req/min vs concurrent sessions. If they mean 15k requests/min = 250 req/sec. With avg 18 tokens => 4500 tokens/sec during peak. We'll need throughput numbers in tokens/sec for sizing.

greg: Quick baseline calc (H100-class perf for quantized medium): ~900 tokens/sec per GPU at typical settings; with batching and short responses we get ~2.5x effective lift. Conservatively assume 1.8x. So nominal per-GPU throughput ~1600 tokens/sec. Peak 4500 -> ~3 GPUs. But we need to account for tail latency SLO and redundancy -> recommend 5 reserved GPUs + 3 burst.

anya: Rationale: reserved pool should cover sustained 95th percentile plus allow one GPU spare for rolling updates. Burst pool (pre-authorized credits) handles sudden small spikes and cache-warmup shortfalls.

tom: They asked about preheat timing and KV cache strategy. Any suggestions?

greg: Preheat plan: 1) warm KV prefix for active user hashes for 15 minutes before predicted peak; 2) issue N synthetic short requests to populate L0 caches across replicas for 5 minutes at increasing RPS; 3) freeze scale-down for critical window. Example: preheat duration 900s + synthetic ramp 300s. Note provisioning lag: dedicated GPUs take ~10-12 minutes to attach and warm; burst spots ~2-6 minutes.

anya: Autoscale policy suggestion (YAML snippet):
```yaml
autoscale:
  reserved_replicas: 5
  burst_credits: 3
  max_replicas: 12
  min_replicas: 5
  target_token_throughput: 1600 # tokens/sec per gpu (target)
  scale_up_window_s: 60
  scale_down_window_s: 180
  cooldown_up_s: 60
  cooldown_down_s: 240
  prefer_reserved: true
  disable_scale_down_windows: ["critical-ops"]
```
Note: tune target_token_throughput per model/quantization.

greg: Batching config recommendations: max_batch_size 64 for chat, prefer dynamic batching with max_latency_ms 30. Also enable prefix-based KV caching for session continuity.

security: Zenith's security questionnaire asks about encryption in transit/at-rest, KMS customer-managed keys, FIPS mode, and audit log export to their S3. We support CMKs via KMS and can enable FIPS for Private deployments. Audit logs can be exported; retention terms negotiable (default 90 days, enterprise + DPA 1 year).

sales-ops: Pricing options: 12-month reserved for 5 GPUs -> 25% off on-demand + 120 burst-credits/month (each credit = 1 GPU-minute at burst spec). Add-ons: FIPS-enabled HSM cluster (+4% infra), extended audit retention (12 months) + compliance support (+3% recurring). I'll draft a quote with line items.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Preheat job created: zenith-preheat-2402233600 by greg (status: queued)

tom: Can we include a minimal runbook for them to run against the dedicated VPC? Need load generator, KV preheat, and emergency fallback.

greg: Runbook (paste into ticket):
```bash
# loadtest (from their infra to our VPC endpoint)
curl -s -X POST https://dedicated-zenith.redwood/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":12}' &

# simple RPS generator using vegeta (example)
echo '{"method":"POST","url":"https://dedicated-zenith.redwood/v1/generate","body":"{\"prompt\":\"warmup\",\"max_tokens\":12}"}' > targets.json
vegeta attack -targets=targets.json -rate=250 -duration=15m | vegeta report

# server-side KV warmup
redwoodctl preheat --project zenith --prefix "/session/*" --duration 900

# emergency fallback
# 1) switch to quantized-small variant
# 2) enable burst credits
# 3) enable shed-lower-priority-requests
redwoodctl failover --project zenith --variant gpt-small-quant-8bit
```

anya: Also recommend setting an SLA-aligned alert: token_throughput_util > 0.85 sustained for 2 minutes -> page SRE and enable extra burst.

tom: Great. Next steps: sales-ops to include quote + concessions, security to provide FIPS/HSM checklist, ops to schedule preheat window on sign. I will confirm peak patterns with Zenith (they may provide historical traffic). Thanks all. :rocket:
